xanthate.e:
Etymology tree
English xanth-
Proto-Indo-European *-h₂
Proto-Indo-European *-éh₂
Proto-Indo-European *-tós
Proto-Indo-European *-eh₂tos
Proto-Italic *-ātos
Latin -atusbor.
English -ate
English xanthate
From xanth- + -ate (“salt or ester”).

s.d: a salt or ester of xanthic acid

xanthelasma.e: From New Latin xanthelasma, from Ancient Greek ξανθός (xanthós, “yellow”) + ἔλασμα (élasma, “metal plate, foil”).

s.d: xanthoma of the eyelids; occurs chiefly in the elderly
(uncountable) A deposit of cholesterol on the eyelid.
excess carotene in the blood stream; can cause the skin to turn a pale yellow or red color
(uncountable) The occurrence of yellow matter in the blood.
x: Among the latter, incipient nephritis and metabolic anomalies, as xanthemia, arthritis uritica, oxaluria are common.

s.d: any of a class of unstable organic acids containing sulphur

xanthine.e: From international scientific vocabulary, from French xanthine, reflecting New Latin combining forms: xanth- + -ine; ultimately from Ancient Greek ξανθός (xanthós, “yellow”), because xanthine is yellowish-white. By surface analysis, xanth- + -ine.

s.d: crystalline oxidation product of the metabolism of nucleoproteins; precursor of uric acid; found in many organs and in urine
(uncountable) Any of a group of alkaloids that include caffeine, theophylline, and theobromine as well as the parent compound, a precursor of uric acid found in many organs of the body.

xanthoma.e:
Etymology tree
English xanth-
Proto-Indo-European *-yéti
Proto-Indo-European *-oyétider.?
Ancient Greek -όω (-óō)
Proto-Indo-European *-mn̥
Proto-Hellenic *-mə
Ancient Greek -μᾰ (-mă)
Ancient Greek -ωμα (-ōma)der.
English -oma
English xanthoma
From xanth- + -oma.

s.d: a skin problem marked by the development (on the eyelids and neck and back) of irregular yellow nodules; sometimes attributable to disturbances of cholesterol metabolism
A small, yellow nodule, rich in cholesterol and other lipids, that occurs in the skin, often near a joint
rare chronic xanthoma of adults in which orange or brownish papules develop on many surfaces of the body
widespread xanthomas (especially on elbows and knees); often associated with a disorder of lipid metabolism

xanthomatosis.e: From xanthoma + -osis. By surface analysis, xanth- + -omatosis.

s.d: widespread xanthomas (especially on elbows and knees); often associated with a disorder of lipid metabolism
(uncountable) A disorder in which excess lipid accumulates in the body and produces xanthomas

xanthomonad.e: From xantho- + monad, from Latin monas (“one, unity”).

s.d: bacteria producing yellow non-water-soluble pigments; some pathogenic for plants
Any of the genus Xanthomonas of proteobacteria.
yellow carotenoid pigments in plants and animal fats and egg yolks
(US, uncountable) Dated spelling of xanthophyll.
yellow carotenoid pigments in plants and animal fats and egg yolks
Any of various hydroxy, carbonyl or carboxylic acid derivatives of carotenes.
(uncountable) Lutein.
visual defect in which objects appear to have a yellowish hue; sometimes occurs in cases of jaundice
(uncountable) A visual defect, a form of chromatopsia in which everything appears yellow.

xanthosis.e:
Etymology tree
English xanth-
Ancient Greek -τῐς (-tĭs)
Ancient Greek -σῐς (-sĭs)
Ancient Greek -ωσις (-ōsis)bor.
New Latin -ōsislbor.
English -osis
English xanthosis
From xanth- + -osis.

s.d: an abnormal yellow discoloration of the skin
(uncountable) A yellowish discolouration of tissues undergoing degeneration.
(uncountable) Synonym of citrinitas.
of the color intermediate between green and orange in the color spectrum; of something resembling the color of an egg yolk
Yellow-brown; yolk-colored.
x: Absorbent fatty xanthous histiocytes and xanthous granulations are observed in the marginal area of necrosis of the fatty tissue[…]

s.d: (archaic) Pertaining to people with yellowish, red, auburn, or brown hair.
x: The xanthous variety springs up out of every black-haired race.
[…] the xanthous, or fair class, comprises those who have brown, auburn, yellow, flaxen, or red hair; […]
